mainTopic: Combining separate eatings within כדי אכילת פרס: רבי מאיר and חכמים, the refutation of רבנאי, and the rules of impure food, immersion, a pregnant woman and a nursing baby
overview: The גמרא first proves from the exact wording of חכמים in the משנה ('עד שישהא') that רבי מאיר's ruling is a stringency. Next, רבנאי quotes שמואל: for חלבים and נבילה, the whole כזית must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס. For impure foods and liquids, the eating counts even over a whole day. רב פפא explains this to mean that each כזית must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס. A ברייתא then says that separate eatings of impure food or drink combine only if the time from the first bite to the last fits within כדי אכילת פרס, and רבנאי is refuted. The גמרא goes on to explain other lines of that ברייתא. Immersing in the middle of eating is forbidden, so a person won't rely on an immersion that doesn't count. A pregnant woman may eat in small portions, even a lot in total, because of danger. The ברייתא also says the baby of an impure nursing mother stays pure. רב נחמן's explanation for this is rejected by רבא, who says the baby is pure because of a double doubt about the amount he drank and the time it took. Finally, the גמרא challenges רבא's view that a woman's milk is like a spring and needs no הכשר, and begins quoting a ברייתא about a זב's liquids that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The wording of חכמים fits if רבי מאיר is being strict
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר is strict, then the wording of חכמים, 'עד שישהא', makes good sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say רבי מאיר is being strict. That is why the משנה says חכמים hold 'unless he spends', meaning he is not liable unless the time he spends is within the time of eating a half-loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof from the wording of the משנה. It shows that one reading of רבי מאיר fits the words of חכמים smoothly. This sets up the next step, where the other reading will not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר is strict (liable even if the eating is spread over a long time), then חכמים are the lenient side. They add a condition before someone becomes liable. The phrase 'עד שישהא' (he is not liable unless he finishes within the time limit) is exactly how you would word a condition for liability.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well / it makes sense (used to set up a contrast)
As a stringency
Unless he spends (time), a condition for being liable
The time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, the standard time limit for one act of eating

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְחוּמְרָא,
phrases.english: It works well if you say that Rabbi Meir ruled as a stringency,
phrases.notes: Strict here means he is liable even if he spread the כזית over a long time.

phrases.english: that is why it teaches: 'unless he spends',

phrases.aramaic: עַד דִּשְׁהִיָּ[ה] דִּילֵיהּ כְּדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.english: meaning: unless his time spent is within the time of eating a half-loaf.
phrases.notes: Some versions add the letter in square brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier question (before this text) of whether רבי מאיר is strict or lenient, starting the proof from wording.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר's ruling is a stringency
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of חכמים in the משנה: 'עד שישהא'

steps.title: If רבי מאיר were lenient, חכמים should have used different words
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר were lenient, חכמים would have said 'אם שהה' (if he spent longer), not 'עד שישהא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say רבי מאיר is being lenient, then the משנה should have said: 'And חכמים say: if he spent (too long), he is exempt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the other reading, that רבי מאיר is lenient. It shows that this reading does not fit the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר were lenient, חכמים would be the strict side. Their natural wording would then be an exemption clause: 'if he spent more than the time limit, he is exempt.' The משנה uses 'until' wording instead, which matches a condition for liability, not an exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: As a leniency
If he spent (too long), wording that points to an exemption
He should have said

steps.confusionAlert: Lenient here would mean רבי מאיר exempts someone who stops in the middle. Strict and lenient describe רבי מאיר's view, and חכמים are always the opposite side.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְקוּלָּא,
phrases.english: But if you say that Rabbi Meir ruled as a leniency,
it should have said: 'And the Rabbis say: If he spent (longer)'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the בשלמא proof: the other option clashes with the wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי מאיר is lenient
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר were lenient, חכמים would be strict and should have worded their view as an exemption ('אם שהה'), not as a condition ('עד שישהא').

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי מאיר is being strict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי מאיר's ruling is a stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: So, must we not learn from this that רבי מאיר is being strict? Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the wording proof and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'עד שישהא' only fits if חכמים are the lenient side. So רבי מאיר is the strict one: he holds one is liable for a כזית even if the eating is spread over a long time.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that...
Learn from it, a confirmed conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר is strict, liable even over a long time. חכמים require the כזית to be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it correct to learn from it:
that Rabbi Meir ruled as a stringency?
Learn from it, that is correct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof built in steps 1 and 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר's ruling is a חומרא.

steps.title: שמואל's rules for forbidden foods and for impure foods
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that for חלבים and נבילה the time limit is כדי אכילת פרס. For impure foods, שקצים, רמשים and liquids the eating counts even over a whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנאי said in the name of שמואל: with forbidden fats and with נבילה, he is liable only if the time from start to finish is within the time of eating a half-loaf. With impure foods, שקצים, רמשים and liquids, it counts even over the whole day, within the time of eating a half-loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching: שמואל gives practical rules for how long eating may be spread out, for different kinds of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חלבים and נבילה, שמואל follows חכמים: the whole כזית must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס. For impure foods, שקצים, רמשים and liquids, he says 'even the whole day' but also mentions 'כדי אכילת פרס'. That sounds like a contradiction, and the next step asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fats
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Ritually impure foods (eating them makes a person impure for תרומה)
Repulsive creatures and creeping creatures
Liquids (here, impure liquids)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical הלכה: the time limit of חכמים applies to forbidden foods.

phrases.english: Ravnai said that Shmuel said:
With forbidden fats and with a carcass, unless he spends,

phrases.aramaic: מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.english: from beginning to end, within the time of eating a half-loaf.
Impure foods, repulsive creatures, creeping creatures, and liquids:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.english: even the entire day, within the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the מחלוקת, the גמרא brings an אמורא's practical ruling on the time limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חלבים and נבילה: within כדי אכילת פרס from start to finish. Impure foods, שקצים, רמשים and liquids: even over a whole day, with a פרס qualifier.

steps.title: What does שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'the whole day' fits with 'within כדי אכילת פרס'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל's last line seems to contradict itself and asks what he means. This sets up רב פפא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even the whole day' and 'within the time of eating a half-loaf' seem to pull in opposite directions. The question asks for the right way to read the two together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (a request to explain unclear wording)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of שמואל's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 'the whole day' and 'כדי אכילת פרס' fit together

steps.title: רב פפא: the whole day, as long as each כזית is within the time limit
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains: the eating may stretch over a whole day, as long as each כזית was eaten within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said, this is what he means: even over the whole day, as long as he ate each כזית within the time of eating a half-loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by showing that the two parts of שמואל's statement talk about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The whole day' refers to the total amount he eats, which may be spread out over the day. 'Within כדי אכילת פרס' refers to each single כזית, which must be eaten within the time limit. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
Provided that, a condition
An olive's size, a basic amount for eating

steps.whatToRemember: For impure foods, the total amount can be eaten over a whole day, but each כזית must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said, this is what he means:
even over the entire day,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁאָכַל כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.english: provided that he ate each olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The whole day' is for the total amount; each כזית must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to require the whole half-פרס within the time limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says all impure foods combine to a כחצי פרס. It suggests this means the whole כחצי פרס must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס, which goes against רב פפא's 'whole day' reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'All foods combine to disqualify the body with half a פרס.' Doesn't this mean he ate the half-פרס within the time it takes to eat a פרס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge שמואל as explained by רב פפא. It suggests the ברייתא means the full amount must be eaten inside one time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said only each כזית needs to be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס, so the total could stretch over a day. The ברייתא speaks of foods combining to a כחצי פרס. The simplest reading is that the whole כחצי פרס is eaten within the time limit, which would leave no room for a whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: They combine; separate small eatings are added together into one measure
To make the body unfit to eat תרומה
The volume of half a פרס, the measure for impure foods
The amount of time it takes to eat a פרס
Isn't it so that...? Introduces the reading the challenger is pushing

phrases.english: They raised an objection: All foods combine
phrases.notes: He means impure foods, the same ones שמואל was talking about.

phrases.english: to disqualify the body with half a peras (a quarter-loaf)
phrases.notes: 'Disqualify the body' means the person may not eat תרומה.

phrases.english: What, is it not that he ate the half peras
within the time of eating a peras?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's explanation in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading of שמואל: eating over a whole day counts if each כזית is within כדי אכילת פרס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא seems to require the entire כחצי פרס to be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס, which leaves no room for a whole day.

steps.title: The ברייתא means each כזית within the time limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can be read as requiring only each כזית to be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס, just as רב פפא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means he ate each כזית within the time it takes to eat a פרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the challenge by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never says the whole כחצי פרס must be eaten in one time limit. It can mean each כזית was eaten within כדי אכילת פרס, and those pieces then add up to a כחצי פרס even over a longer time. That fits רב פפא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Each olive-sized piece, one at a time
No; rejects the suggested reading

phrases.english: No, it is where he ate each olive-bulk
within the time of eating a peras.
phrases.notes: So the whole half-פרס could take longer; only each כזית has to be quick.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דַּאֲכַל כְּזַיִת כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא to fit רב פפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole כחצי פרס must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס
steps.terutzMaskana: Only each כזית must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס

steps.title: A second ברייתא says start to finish must fit in the time limit
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא spells it out: if he ate and then ate again, the pieces combine only if the time from the start of the first eating to the end of the last is within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'All foods combine to disqualify the body with half a פרס within the time it takes to eat a פרס. How? He ate and then ate again. If from the start of the first eating until the end of the last eating there is only the time of eating a פרס, they combine. More than that, they do not combine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger ברייתא that seems to make the 'each כזית' answer impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא measures the time from the very first bite to the very last bite, not each כזית by itself. If the whole span is longer than כדי אכילת פרס, the eatings do not combine. That goes directly against eating over a whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? Introduces the explanation of a rule
From the start of the first eating
The end of the last eating
More than this; past the time limit

phrases.english: They raised an objection: All foods combine
to disqualify the body with half a peras
within the time of eating a peras. How so?
He ate and then ate again,
if from the beginning of the first eating
until the end of the last eating
there is the time of eating a peras, they combine,
more than that, they do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new and sharper challenge after the answer in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל as explained by רב פפא, and the 'each כזית' answer of step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא measures from the start of the first eating to the end of the last, so the whole amount must fit within כדי אכילת פרס. It cannot stretch over a day.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: immersing in the middle and a pregnant woman
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds that one may not eat less than the measure, immerse, and then eat more. If he did, the eatings still combine. A pregnant woman is allowed to eat less than the measure because of danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not allow eating less than the measure and then going down to immerse. If he went down, immersed, came up and completed it, it combines. They allowed a pregnant woman to eat less than the measure, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the second ברייתא. These extra details are part of the source, not a new challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing in the middle does not break up the eating. The second part still joins the first if it completes the measure. The pregnant woman's case is a special allowance because of danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the set measure
To immerse in a מקוה
And he completed it, finishing the full measure
A pregnant woman
Because of the danger

phrases.english: They did not permit eating less than the measure
to go down and immerse,
phrases.notes: He means eating a little, immersing, and planning to eat more as if starting fresh.

phrases.english: If he went down, immersed, came up and completed it, it combines.
They permitted a pregnant woman
to eat less than the measure, because of the danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא from step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing between eatings does not stop them from combining. A pregnant woman may eat less than the measure because of danger.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge or a new source. It is still the same ברייתא that began in step 9.

steps.title: The ברייתא gives the same time limit for liquids
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says all impure liquids combine to a רביעית only if the time from the first sip to the last is within כדי אכילת פרס. This goes against שמואל, who said liquids count even over a whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: All liquids combine to disqualify the body with a רביעית within the time it takes to eat a פרס. How? He drank and then drank again. If from the start of the first drinking until the end of the last drinking there is only the time of eating a פרס, they combine. More than that, they do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the second ברייתא, which now gives the same time rule for liquids. The challenge itself comes in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל listed liquids among the things that count over a whole day. This ברייתא gives liquids the same tight limit, measured from the start of the first drink to the end of the last. So the challenge now covers both foods and liquids.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids
A quarter-לוג, the measure for liquids
He drank and then drank again

steps.whatToRemember: The second ברייתא measures from the first bite or sip to the last one, for both foods and liquids. This clashes with שמואל's 'whole day' as רב פפא explained it. Step 13 uses this ברייתא to refute רבנאי.

phrases.english: All liquids combine
to disqualify the body with a quarter-log
within the time of eating a peras. How so?
He drank and then drank again,
if from the beginning of the first drinking
until the end of the last drinking
there is the time of eating a peras, they combine,
more than that, they do not combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמַּשְׁקִין מִצְטָרְפִין לִפְסוֹל אֶת הַגְּוִיָּיה בִּרְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from steps 9-10 and extends the challenge to liquids
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that liquids count even over a whole day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires the whole רביעית to be drunk within כדי אכילת פרס, measured from the start of the first drink to the end of the last.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure liquids combine to a רביעית only if the time from the start of the first drink to the end of the last is within כדי אכילת פרס.

steps.title: A nursing mother who touched a corpse-impure person may nurse her baby
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a leniency: a woman who became impure by touching someone who was טמא מת may nurse her child, and the child stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages allowed a woman who touched someone impure from a corpse to nurse her child, and her child remains pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it started in the earlier steps. This last line adds one more lenient rule, about a nursing mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right before this, the ברייתא allowed a pregnant woman to eat less than the measure because of danger. Here it adds that a mother who is impure from touching a טמא מת may still nurse her baby. The Sages treat the baby as pure, so the impurity does not pass on to the child.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who touched someone who was impure from a corpse
To nurse (a baby)
Pure; not ritually impure

phrases.english: They permitted her, who touched one impure from a corpse,
to nurse her child, and her child is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in steps 9-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nursing mother who is impure from touching a טמא מת may nurse, and the child remains pure.

steps.title: The ברייתא conclusively refutes רבנאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the key line of the ברייתא: the eatings combine only if the time from the start of the first eating to the end of the last is within כדי אכילת פרס. That disproves רבנאי, and the refutation stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches: if from the start of the first eating until the end of the eating it is within the time of eating a פרס, it combines. This is a refutation of רבנאי, a real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the important line in the long ברייתא and uses it to knock down רבנאי's view. It ends by saying the refutation is final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנאי held that the eating could combine even if it was spread out longer, as long as each כזית was eaten within כדי אכילת פרס. The ברייתא says the whole span, from the first bite of the first eating to the end of the last, must fit inside כדי אכילת פרס. There is no answer to this, so the גמרא concludes with תיובתא.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches. This points to the one line of a long source that matters for the argument
Combines; the separate amounts are counted together
A conclusive refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: Separate eatings combine to the measure only if the time from the start of the first eating to the end of the last is within כדי אכילת פרס. רבנאי's looser view is rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'תיובתא, תיובתא' is not just a repeated challenge. Saying it a second time means the refutation is final and the view is dropped.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
if there is, from the start of the first eating
until the end of the eating,
within the time of eating a פרס, it combines.
The refutation of רבנאי is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the ברייתא, the גמרא returns to its key line from step 9 to close the argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבנאי's view that the full span of eating does not have to fit within כדי אכילת פרס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires the whole span, from the first eating to the last, to fit within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבנאי is refuted. Eatings combine only if the entire span falls within כדי אכילת פרס.

steps.title: What does 'they did not permit him to immerse' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that one who ate less than the measure was not allowed to go down and immerse, and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: They did not permit him to eat less than the measure and go down and immerse. What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a confusing line from the ברייתא (step 10) and asks what it means. This sets up רב יהודה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually immersing is a good thing, so it is strange that the Sages would forbid it. Also, someone who ate less than the measure did not become impure at all. The גמרא wants to know what the problem is.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the minimum amount that makes a person impure
To go down into a מקוה and immerse
What is it saying? A request to explain unclear wording

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִתִּירוּ לוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר
phrases.english: They did not permit him to eat less than the measure
and to go down and immerse.
What is it saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: לֹא הִתִּירוּ לוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבנאי has been refuted, the גמרא turns to explain another line of the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Sages would forbid immersion after eating less than the measure, and what the ברייתא's wording means.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the rule stops a person from relying on an immersion that does not count
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that if someone ate less than the measure, immersed, and then ate more to complete the measure, all the eatings combine. The Sages forbade the middle immersion so he would not think it purified him, since only an immersion at the end works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said, this is what it means: if he ate less than the measure, they did not permit him to go down and immerse. Because if he went down, immersed, came up, and completed the measure, it combines. He might come to say, 'My first immersion helped me,' and he does not know that immersion only works at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from the last step. He explains that the ban on immersing is a safeguard against a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing in the middle does not stop the first and second eatings from combining, as long as they fall within כדי אכילת פרס. The person might think the early immersion cleared him, but he becomes impure only after finishing, so only a later immersion helps. To prevent this mistake, the Sages did not allow the middle immersion at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Introduces an explanation of unclear wording
He completed it, by eating enough to reach the full measure
It helped me; it was effective for me
The first immersion

steps.whatToRemember: An immersion in the middle of eating does not break up the eatings, so they still combine. Only an immersion after the last eating purifies, and the Sages banned the middle immersion so no one would rely on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rabbis making a protective rule against a likely mistake, not because the immersion itself is harmful.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said, this is what it means:
if he ate less than the measure,
they did not permit him to go down and immerse,
because if he went down, immersed, and came up
and completed it, it combines.
phrases.notes: He means he ate more impure food to complete the full measure, all within the time limit.

phrases.english: And he would come to say:
'The first immersion helped me,'
and he does not know
that immersion only works at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on immersion is a safeguard. A middle immersion does not stop the eatings from combining, and the person might wrongly think it purified him, when only an immersion at the end works.

steps.title: Why only less than the measure if there is danger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that a pregnant woman may eat less than the measure because of danger. It challenges this: if there is danger, she should be allowed to eat even a lot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא taught: they allowed a pregnant woman to eat less than the measure because of the danger. But if it is because of danger, let her eat even a lot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the same ברייתא and attacks it. If danger is the reason, why limit her to less than the measure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Danger to life overrides the prohibition completely. So a limit of 'less than the measure' seems to make no sense. If she needs food, she should be allowed to eat as much as she needs.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant woman
Less than the amount the law counts as a real eating
Because of danger to life
A lot, a large amount

phrases.english: It taught: they permitted a pregnant woman
to eat less than the measure
because of the danger.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי הַסַּכָּנָה אֲפִילּוּ טוּבָא נָמֵי תֵּיכוֹל!
phrases.english: If it is because of the danger, let her eat even a lot!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי הַסַּכָּנָה אֲפִילּוּ טוּבָא נָמֵי תֵּיכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the immersion line (steps 14-15) to the next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's wording that permits the pregnant woman only 'less than the measure'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Danger overrides the prohibition entirely, so a limit on the amount seems pointless.

steps.title: רב פפא: small portions, even if the total is a lot
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rereads the ברייתא: she is allowed to eat in portions of less than the measure, even if all together she eats a lot, because of the danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this is what it means. They allowed a pregnant woman to eat less than the measure at a time, even if she eats a lot in total, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by explaining what 'less than the measure' really means. It describes how she eats, not how much she eats in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'less than the measure' are not a limit on the total. She eats small portions spaced apart so they do not combine into one full eating. She may keep doing this even until she has eaten a lot, because of the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it teaches': a rereading of the text's wording

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'less than the measure' as a cap on how much she may eat. It means she eats in small separate portions, and the total can be large.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: this is what it teaches:
they permitted a pregnant woman less than the measure,
phrases.notes: He means each portion is less than the measure, eaten far enough apart that they don't add up together.

phrases.english: even a lot, because of the danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Less than the measure' was understood as a limit on the total amount she may eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Less than the measure' describes eating in small separate portions, and she may eat a lot this way.

steps.title: Why does the nursing baby stay pure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's leniency that a woman who touched a טמא מת may nurse and her son stays pure. It asks: the baby drinks her milk, so he should become impure from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא taught: they allowed a woman who touched a טמא מת to nurse her son, and her son is pure. Why is he pure? Once he drinks the milk, he should become impure from the milk!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last line of the ברייתא (from step 12) and challenges it. The mother is impure, so her milk should be impure, and the baby should become impure by drinking it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother became impure by touching someone who was a טמא מת. Her milk touches her, so it should become impure. The baby who drinks impure milk should then become impure too, which contradicts the ברייתא saying he is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who touched a person made impure by a dead body
To nurse a baby
He becomes impure

phrases.english: It taught: they permitted one who touched a person impure from a corpse
to nurse her son,
and her son is pure.
Why is he pure?
Once he nurses the milk,
he becomes impure from the milk!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the final line of the ברייתא, first mentioned in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the nursing baby stays pure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The impure mother makes her milk impure, and drinking impure milk should make the baby impure.

steps.title: Blocking the answer that the milk was never made susceptible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא anticipates a defense: maybe the milk never became susceptible to impurity. It rejects this, because the smeared drop on the nipple makes it susceptible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the milk was not made susceptible to impurity, it was made susceptible by the smeared drop on the tip of the nipple!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its question by closing off an easy way out. It says the milk did become able to receive impurity, because of a drop left on the nipple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become impure after it has been made wet by a liquid (הכשר). One might say the milk, as the baby's food, never got that wetting. The גמרא answers that a drop of milk smeared on the nipple counts as a liquid, and it wets the rest of the milk, so the milk can become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say': raising a possible answer in order to reject it
Was made susceptible to impurity (from הֶכְשֵׁר)
A smeared drop that stays on the surface
Nipple, breast

steps.confusionAlert: Food does not become impure just by touching something impure; it must first be made wet by a liquid (הכשר). That is why the גמרא has to show how the milk got 'wet'.

phrases.english: And if you say: it was not made susceptible,
it was made susceptible by a smeared drop
on the tip of the nipple!
phrases.notes: That leftover drop isn't swallowed as food, so it counts as a liquid, and it wets the milk that flows past it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 18 by rejecting a possible defense ahead of time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible defense that the milk never received הכשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The smeared drop on the nipple acts as a liquid that makes the milk susceptible, so the milk can become impure.

steps.title: One strong suck leaves no drop
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה answers that the baby sucked in one strong pull, so no smeared drop was left on the nipple.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the case is where the baby sucked in one strong pull, and did not leave a smeared drop on the tip of the nipple.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers by limiting the ברייתא to a specific case. The baby sucked so strongly that no drop was left behind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no drop stays on the nipple, nothing counts as a liquid to make the milk susceptible. So the milk can't become impure, and the baby stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: One strong pull or suck

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
With one strong suck,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִנִּיחַ טִיפָּה מְלוּכְלֶכֶת עַל פִּי הַדַּד.
phrases.english: he did not leave a smeared drop on the tip of the nipple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: בִּתְקִיפָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 18-19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nursing always leaves a drop on the nipple, which makes the milk susceptible and impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of one strong suck that leaves no drop, so the milk never became susceptible.

steps.title: רבא: two problems with the one-suck answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב נחמן's answer with two arguments: a baby's mouth is visibly full of milk, and the source of the milk is like a spring, so it needs no wetting at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: there are two answers against this. One, we see that the baby's mouth is full of milk! And furthermore, the place of the milk is a spring.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down רב נחמן's answer from two sides. So the question of why the baby stays pure comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, we can see the baby's mouth fill with milk, so he never swallows it all at once without leaving any behind. Second, milk inside the body is like a spring, part of the woman herself, so it does not need הכשר; if she is impure, her milk is impure. Either way, the 'no drop' answer does not save the baby's purity.

keyTerms.meaning: Two refutations, two arguments against
A baby, infant
A spring, a natural source of water

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's second point is the stronger one: milk is like a spring, so it doesn't need הכשר at all. That undoes the whole 'smeared drop' discussion, and the question of the baby's purity comes back. רבא gives his own answer in step 24.

phrases.english: Rava said: there are two refutations of this matter:
One, that we see the mouth of the baby
that it is full of milk!
phrases.notes: So he can't be swallowing everything in one pull. Milk is left over, and some stays on the nipple.

phrases.english: And furthermore, the place of the milk is a spring.
phrases.notes: Milk is treated as part of the woman's body, so it doesn't need to get wet first in order to become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב נחמן's 'one strong suck' answer completely, reopening the question of step 18.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In reality a drop is always left, and in any case milk is like a spring and needs no הכשר to become impure.

steps.title: A משנה about a woman's milk
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה: a woman's milk makes food susceptible to טומאה whether it came out wanted or not. An animal's milk does so only when it came out wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the משנה teaches: a woman's milk makes food susceptible to impurity whether it came out wanted or unwanted. An animal's milk makes food susceptible only if it came out wanted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his claim that the milk's source is like a spring by quoting a משנה. This step sets up the inference he draws in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a liquid makes food susceptible to טומאה only if it came out in a way the owner wanted. The משנה says a woman's milk works even when it was not wanted. That points to a special status for her milk, which רבא will use in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's milk
Here: makes food able to become impure (counts as a liquid that prepares food for טומאה)
Wanted, coming out with approval
An animal

steps.confusionAlert: Here מְטַמֵּא does not mean the milk itself makes things impure. It means the milk counts as a liquid that makes food able to become impure later.

phrases.english: As it is taught: a woman's milk makes food susceptible to impurity
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מכשירין, about liquids that prepare food to be able to become impure.

phrases.english: whether it came out wanted or not wanted,
(an animal's milk makes food susceptible only when it came out wanted.)
phrases.notes: These words are in round brackets, so some versions leave them out here.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָתָנֵי: חֲלֵב אִשָּׁה מְטַמֵּא בֵּין לְרָצוֹן וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבא's second argument in step 21, that the milk's source is like a spring.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the place of the milk is like a spring and needs no wetting
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מכשירין: a woman's milk makes food susceptible whether wanted or not

steps.title: Unwanted milk still counts
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'not wanted' as milk that is not welcome at all, yet the משנה still says it makes food susceptible. So a woman's milk has a special status.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't 'not wanted' mean the milk is not welcome to him at all? Yet the משנה still says it makes food susceptible to impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws his conclusion from the משנה. Even unwanted milk counts, so a woman's milk acts like a spring and needs nothing extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary liquids only count if they came out wanted. Since a woman's milk counts even when unwanted, it is not treated like an ordinary liquid. Its source works like a spring, so it makes no difference whether a smeared drop was left on the nipple. רב נחמן's 'one strong suck' answer fails, and the question from step 18 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't it mean...? (a way of offering a reading as obvious)
It is welcome or acceptable to him

steps.whatToRemember: A woman's milk counts as a liquid even when it is unwanted, so רבא treats its source like a spring that needs no outside wetting.

phrases.english: Doesn't 'not wanted' mean
that it is not welcome to him at all,
and yet it teaches that it makes food susceptible to impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן דְּלָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 22, finishing the rejection of רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman's milk needs no הכשר, so רב נחמן's answer fails
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase 'שלא לרצון' in the משנה, read as fully unwanted milk

steps.title: רבא's own reason: a double doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the baby stays pure because of doubt. Maybe he did not drink the full measure. Even if he did, maybe he did not drink it within the time of אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: this is why her son is pure. It is uncertain whether he nursed the full measure or not. And even if you say he did, it is uncertain whether he nursed it within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf, or over a longer time.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב נחמן's answer was rejected, רבא gives a new answer to the question from step 18. The baby is pure because we are not sure he drank enough impure milk in the required time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא admits the milk is impure. The baby only becomes impure if he drinks a full measure within the time of אכילת פרס. There are two layers of doubt, the amount and the speed, and with that doubt the baby is treated as pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt, an uncertain case
The required measure (amount)
The time it takes to eat a half-loaf; the time window for combining amounts
Even if you say; granting the first point

steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the reason for the baby's purity away from the physics of the milk and onto the rules of measure and doubt.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
this is the reason her son is pure:
because it is uncertain whether he nursed the full measure
or did not nurse it,
and even if you say he did nurse it,
it is uncertain whether he nursed it within the time of eating a half-loaf,

phrases.aramaic: סְפֵק יְנָקוֹ בְּיוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.english: or whether he nursed it over more than the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דִּבְנָהּ טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב נחמן's rejected answer (step 20) with a new answer to the question of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasts the case as a doubt about measure and time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The baby drank impure milk, so he should be impure
steps.terutzMaskana: The baby is pure because it is a double doubt whether he drank a full measure within כדי אכילת פרס

steps.title: Questioning רבא's view of the milk's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, according to רבא, the place of the milk really is a spring that needs no הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, is the place of the milk a spring, so that it does not need הכשר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the idea רבא used to reject רב נחמן. This line sets up a challenge that the גמרא will develop next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the milk's source is like a spring, so the milk needs no wetting to become susceptible to טומאה. The גמרא is about to test whether that claim really holds. If it does not, רבא's rejection of רב נחמן gets weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: The place the milk comes from
A spring; a source that counts as a liquid on its own
Wetting by a liquid that makes something able to become impure

phrases.english: And according to Rava, the place of the milk is a spring,
and it does not need preparation for impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרָבָא, מְקוֹם חָלָב מַעְיָין הוּא, וְלֹא צָרִיךְ הֶכְשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to examine the spring idea רבא used in steps 21 to 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the place of the milk is like a spring and needs no הכשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Questions whether the milk's source really has the status of a spring; the full challenge comes next

steps.title: Milk dripping into an oven shows that a woman's milk needs הכשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה: milk dripping from a woman into an oven's airspace makes the oven impure. רבי יוחנן explains that the milk became susceptible through the wet drop on the tip of the breast. So a woman's milk does need הכשר, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: a woman whose milk dripped from her breasts into the airspace of an oven makes the oven impure. We asked: how did that milk become susceptible to טומאה? רבי יוחנן answered: through the wet drop that sits on the tip of the breast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for the question it just asked in step 25. It shows that a woman's milk is not like a spring that needs no הכשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the source of the milk were like a spring, nobody would need to explain how the milk became susceptible. Yet the גמרא asked exactly that question, and רבי יוחנן had to find a wet drop on the outside of the breast to answer it. So according to רבי יוחנן, a woman's milk does need הכשר, which clashes with רבא's argument in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: The airspace inside an oven. An earthenware vessel becomes impure when something impure enters its airspace.
It became susceptible, meaning it got the הכשר that lets it receive טומאה.
A wet, smeared drop sitting on the tip of the breast.
Breast or nipple.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source against רבא. If רבי יוחנן's view stands, רבא's claim in step 21 that the milk's source is a spring falls apart.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: a woman whose milk dripped from her breasts
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in כלים 8:11.

phrases.english: and it fell into the airspace of an oven, the oven is impure.
And it was difficult for us: through what did it become susceptible?
phrases.notes: Food or drink can only pick up טומאה after it has been made susceptible, so the question is how this milk got that status.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: through the smeared drop
on the tip of the breast.
phrases.notes: That drop is already wet on the outside, so it serves as the wetting that makes the milk susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the question in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim in step 21 that the source of a woman's milk is like a spring and needs no הכשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן needed a wet drop on the breast to explain how the milk became susceptible. That shows a woman's milk does need הכשר.

steps.title: רבא cannot simply disagree with רבי יוחנן, because a ברייתא lists the liquids of a זב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא heads off the reply that רבא just disagrees with רבי יוחנן. It begins quoting a ברייתא about nine liquids of a זב. It starts with sweat, pus and excrement, which are completely pure, and then moves on to tears and blood from a wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that רבא does not hold like רבי יוחנן, wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: You find that there are nine liquids of a זב. Sweat, foul pus and excrement are pure from everything. The tears of his eye and the blood of his wound...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks an escape route for רבא and starts bringing a ברייתא as a source. The ברייתא's list continues in the next lines, so this step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One אמורא may disagree with another, so רבא could have simply argued with רבי יוחנן. To close that option, the גמרא brings a ברייתא, and an אמורא cannot argue with a ברייתא. Here we only see the start of the list: some liquids of a זב are fully pure, and the list then moves on to other liquids.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. This introduces a possible answer that the גמרא is about to reject.
A man who is impure because of a discharge. Some of his bodily fluids carry טומאה.
Liquids.
Foul-smelling pus or discharge.
Pure from everything. They do not become impure and do not make anything susceptible.

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is not finished on this amud. The line that matters for the question against רבא comes as the list continues on the next amud.
